translations.source_sense_description: Unteroffizier bei der Marine oder der Wasserschutzpolizei

glosses: A fellow, comrade, colleague, partner or someone with whom something is shared, e.g. shipmate, classmate.

examples.text: A "mate" was a "mate" - share and share alike, no matter how bad might be the times, or how long a spell of ill luck had attended them.

glosses: A breeding partner.

examples.text: Such overt displays of avowed sexual prowess – or at least, desperate availability – are not limited to the countryside. Even in the city, birds and animals and stockbrokers and nurses find ways of signalling their suitability as a mate.

glosses: A friend, usually of the same sex.

examples.text: I'm going to the pub with a few mates.

glosses: Friendly term of address to a stranger, usually male, of similar age.

examples.text: Excuse me, mate, have you got the time?

glosses: In naval ranks, a non-commissioned officer or his subordinate (e.g. Boatswain's Mate, Gunner's Mate, Sailmaker's Mate, etc).
A ship's officer, subordinate to the master on a commercial ship.
A first mate.
A technical assistant in certain trades (e.g. gasfitter's mate, plumber's mate); sometimes an apprentice.
The other member of a matched pair of objects.

examples.text: I found one of the socks I wanted to wear, but I couldn't find its mate.

glosses: A suitable companion; a match; an equal.

examples.text: Ye knew me once no mate / For you; there sitting where you durst not soar.

glosses: To match, fit together without space between.

examples.text: The pieces of the puzzle mate perfectly.

glosses: To copulate.

examples.text: “In fact, the apes live with us, and have for many ages. We call them the first men—we speak their language quite as much as we do our own; only in the rituals of the temple do we make any attempt to retain our mother tongue. In time it will be forgotten, and we will speak only the language of the apes; in time we will no longer banish those of our people who mate with apes, and so in time we shall descend to the very beasts from which ages ago our progenitors may have sprung.”

glosses: To pair in order to raise offspring.
To arrange in matched pairs.
To introduce (animals) together for the purpose of breeding.
To copulate with.
To marry; to match (a person).

examples.text: If she be mated with an equal husband.

glosses: To match oneself against; to oppose as equal; to compete with.

examples.text: There is no passion in the mind of man so weak but it mates and masters the fear of death.
I, […] in the way of loyalty and truth, […] / Dare mate a sounder man than Surrey can be.

glosses: To fit (objects) together without space between.
To come together as companions, comrades, partners, etc.

examples.text: Indeed, some cases of devotion that were met with were quite touching; and very often to all appearances the pairs were not always mated from the same class of society.

glosses: To move (a space shuttle orbiter) onto the back of an aircraft that can carry it.
Clipping of checkmate.
Clipping of checkmate.
To confuse; to confound.

examples.text: I think you are all mated, or stark mad.

glosses: Alternative spelling of maté, an aromatic tea-like drink prepared from the holly yerba maté (Ilex paraguariensis).
The abovementioned plant; the leaves and shoots used for the tea
